title: Impact of Short Sale Ban on Financial Stock Volatility

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with stock (unit) and period fixed effects.  

Why: The research design has two dimensions that vary independently—treatment status (stocks subject to the ban vs. not) and time (before vs. after the ban). DID isolates the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) by comparing the change in log-volatility for banned stocks to the change for non-banned stocks.  

Key assumptions  
• Parallel-trends: In the absence of the ban, the treated and control stocks would have followed the same trend in log-volatility.  
• No spillovers or anticipation: Non-treated stocks are not indirectly affected, and treated stocks did not adjust volatility prior to the formal ban date.  
• Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA) and no composition changes across periods.  

## 2. R Code
```r
#------------------------------------------------------------
# Impact of Short-Sale Ban on Financial Stock Volatility
#------------------------------------------------------------
# Required packages
if (!requireNamespace("fixest", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("fixest")
if (!requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("data.table")

library(fixest)      # fast high-dimensional fixed-effect estimation
library(data.table)  # efficient data handling

# 1. Read data --------------------------------------------------------------
file_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s43_data.csv"
dt <- fread(file_path)

# Quick sanity check
print(head(dt))

# 2. Baseline DID with two-way FE ------------------------------------------
# Model: y_it = α_i + δ_t + β * (treated_i × post_t) + ε_it
did_base <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,      # two-way fixed effects
  data = dt,
  cluster = ~unit_id                        # cluster SEs at the stock level
)

cat("\n--- Baseline DID result ---\n")
print(summary(did_base, cluster = "unit_id")$coeftable)

# 3. Robustness check 1: No fixed effects (simple DID) ----------------------
did_simple <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = dt)

cat("\n--- Simple DID (no FE) result ---\n")
print(coef(summary(did_simple))["treat_x_post", ])

# 4. Robustness check 2: Event-study leads/lags ----------------------------
# We estimate dynamic effects to gauge pre-trends. Assume period is integer
# and event time = period - first_post_period
# First, create relative time dummies (Sun & Abraham style)
# Identify the first period that is 'post' for each treated unit
dt[, first_post := min(period[post == 1]), by = unit_id]
dt[, rel_time := period - first_post]

# Keep relative times within a window [-3, +3] for illustration
dt[, rel_grp := fifelse(rel_time <= -4, -4,
                 fifelse(rel_time >=  4,  4, rel_time))]

# Interact relative time with treated indicator
event_mod <- feols(
  y ~ sunab(treated, rel_time) | unit_id + period,
  data = dt,
  cluster = ~unit_id
)

cat("\n--- Event-study summary (Sun & Abraham) ---\n")
print(etable(event_mod, se.bare = "cluster"))

# 5. Output the key ATT estimate -------------------------------------------
att_coef  <- coef(did_base)["treat_x_post"]
att_se    <- se(did_base)["treat_x_post"]
cat("\n*** Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT):\n")
cat(sprintf("Coefficient (β̂) = %.4f, Clustered SE = %.4f\n", att_coef, att_se))
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Economic intuition suggests that banning short selling reduces trading activity that exploits negative information, thereby lowering contemporaneous volatility in the targeted stocks. Hence:  

Sign: Negative.  
Approximate magnitude: A decline of about 0.10–0.25 log-points in volatility (β̂ ≈ −0.15), which translates to an  ≈ 14%–22% reduction in raw volatility levels.  

Robustness checks should confirm no significant pre-trend and a stable, negative post-ban effect.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log stock volatility between treated and untreated stocks before and after the ban.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The short selling ban led to a reduction in log stock volatility for the treated financial stocks.
